caption: Brendan Ngehsi Newanforbi v. AT&T Mobility Services LLC, et al.
court: San Joaquin Sup. Ct. (proposed; review draft not filed)
claims: Penal Code § 290.46(j); FCRA § 1681b(b)(3); ICRAA §§ 1786.40, 1786.50; Breach of Contract; Implied Covenant; Promissory Estoppel; Negligent Misrepresentation; Fraud / Concealment; UCL § 17200 (alternative pleading)
status: UNEXECUTED REVIEW DRAFT — A nine-count verified complaint is prepared for proposed execution September 8, 2026 against AT&T Mobility Services LLC and First Advantage Background Services Corp. It pleads registry-use, FCRA, and ICRAA theories on information and belief from the two-hour offer-rescission chronology and First Advantage’s documented 2024 registry match to Plaintiff, with independent offer-based claims pleaded in the alternative. It is deliberately unsigned and must not be filed until Plaintiff personally confirms offer acceptance, onboarding/screening completion, each alleged act of reliance, economic loss, and nonreceipt of pre-adverse materials. No CRD charge/right-to-sue appears in the record, so FEHA and Fair Chance counts are preserved but not included.

key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific (5756 Pacific Ave. #94, Stockton) at 1:15 p.m., and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi (2439 W. Kettleman Ln.) at 2:31 p.m. AT&T immediately advanced both applications. The Stockton track generated a Virtual Job Tryout and an interview invitation; the Lodi track generated an interview invitation. The original Stockton interview was set for May 19 at 4:45 p.m. but was canceled at 3:46 p.m. that day and rescheduled for May 22 at 10:30 a.m. The original Lodi interview was set for May 20 at 2:00 p.m. but was canceled at 1:51 p.m. and rescheduled for May 21 at 2:00 p.m. Reminder emails document the rescheduled appointments, but the exhibits do not independently prove attendance or what was said in either interview. On May 22 at 11:11 a.m., AT&T’s language-testing provider directed Plaintiff to complete a pre-employment assessment within five days for Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant position 16000025. At 11:37 a.m., Language Testing International provided access code 82594911 for an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish speaking test expiring May 25 at midnight and stated that the rating would be provided to AT&T Taleo. The file does not include the test recording, score, proficiency threshold, score report, retest policy as applied, or evidence of who reviewed the result. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., AT&T Workday sent “Welcome to the team,” stating it was “excited to officially offer” Plaintiff R-106742 and directing him to review and accept the formal offer in Candidate Home. Workday then sent offer-process tasks at 10:15, 10:16, and 10:17 a.m. to review documents, change government identifiers, and change personal information. At 10:19 a.m., First Advantage stated that “AT&T Non Management” had contracted for screening services and invited Plaintiff to provide information, review FCRA rights, and optionally complete ID.me identity verification. At 12:23 p.m., a text shown under recruiter Richard Patterson’s AT&T contact stated: “Unfortunately, the manager advised me that he no longer wants to move forward with your offer. He stated that he need a Spanish speaker and you did not pass the Spanish assessment. Sorry for the inconvenience.” Plaintiff replied: “No worries sir, thank you for the opportunity.” The sequence proves an offer followed by an almost immediate rescission and an express stated reason. It does not prove that Plaintiff opened or accepted the formal offer, completed onboarding or screening, incurred reliance expenses, left other work, lost alternative employment, or received any First Advantage report or adverse-action notice.
procedural_status: Verified complaint review draft generated for proposed September 8, 2026 execution; deliberately unsigned and unfiled. Pre-execution gates: (1) add/inspect complete Workday offer; (2) confirm exact acceptance method/time; (3) confirm which onboarding and First Advantage tasks Plaintiff completed; (4) identify each concrete act of reliance and alternative job/opportunity; (5) confirm no pre-adverse report or rights summary arrived through any email/portal; (6) verify factual allegations under penalty of perjury; and (7) verify current California agents for service. Discovery targets remain the AT&T Workday audit, R-106742/R-107776 disposition history, LTI score/transmission, Patterson/manager communications, and the individual First Advantage order under client account 132156. No CRD charge or right-to-sue is recorded.
damages: User reports the written offer specified $24.95/hour plus targeted variable compensation and a tentative June 15, 2026 start. At 40 hours, base pay would be $998/week, but the record does not establish scheduled weekly hours, acceptance, reliance loss, mitigation period, or expected duration. Statutory remedies are contingent: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) permits actual/treble relief with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty up to $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 permits actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus specified relief; FCRA remedies depend on negligent or willful violation. Portfolio valuation remains $0 until acceptance/reliance or report use is confirmed.
risk: High-risk review draft, not filing-ready. The complaint maximizes independent paths but cannot manufacture the missing facts. The § 290.46/FCRA/ICRAA counts may be dismissed if First Advantage had not completed or transmitted a report before 12:23 p.m.; the invitation alone proves an order/task, not report use. Contract, implied-covenant, estoppel, and misrepresentation counts may fail without personal confirmation and documentary proof of acceptance, reliance, and loss. Fraud remains vulnerable without internal knowledge/intent facts; UCL standing/remedies require actual lost money/property and no adequate legal remedy. FEHA/Fair Chance counts are omitted absent exhaustion. The likely employer is AT&T Mobility Services LLC based on Mobility labor materials, and the likely CRA is First Advantage Background Services Corp.; both must be confirmed before service.
